text:
[IRET.6.4] **Alpha test evaluation.** On fact assert, the
engine evaluates all alpha tests for every alpha node
registered for `fact->schema->id`. Tests short-circuit:
the first failing test skips the fact for that node. A
fact that passes all tests is inserted into the alpha
memory and the downstream beta inputs are notified.

Short-circuiting is sound because every alpha test is **decided**: it answers
`true` or `false` and cannot raise, the only conjuncts the compiler may take out
of a `where` (RLOW.5.5). Rejecting a fact on one therefore cannot change what
the `where` yields ([LNUL.4.2]), for an artefact that does not lie
([LDET.1.11]).

**Two alpha tests are not decided:** one whose `slot_index` names no slot of
the fact's schema ([RDSC.4a.9.1]), and a REGEX test whose subject is not
a `String` ([RDSC.4a.6.2]). Each faults. The engine must not
short-circuit on either. The fact is rejected if another test of the node answers `false`, and
the fault is raised only if none does.

alloy.name: iret_6_4__fstop
alloy.note: What ends the filter phase, in the clause's order: the filters answering false, if any -- a false anywhere rejects, a faulting test beside it notwithstanding; else, with no false among them, the faulting filters T2I selects, [LNUL.4.2]'s pick between two faults the clause reaches through RLOW.5.5 (the tests are hoisted conjuncts); else the filters answering null, the model's own extension on an input the clause never presents (an alpha test is decided for an artefact that does not lie); else none, and every filter passed. Source order never enters; the short-circuit the clause's first paragraph allows over decided tests loses nothing.

alloy.name: iret_6_4__v5_false_rejects
alloy.note: A false among the filters rejects, whatever else they answer -- a faulting test beside it included -- and nothing is recorded, over every set of filters, every order of the rest and every `where` of up to three conjuncts: the clause's first arm, restated as double entry on `iret_6_4__fstop`. Ending the phase at the first filter in source order that is not true breaks it (TEETH).

alloy.name: iret_6_4__v5_fault_if_none_false
alloy.note: With no false among the filters and a fault among them, the evaluation ends on a fault one of the filters raised, whatever the rest would answer, and records that fault's atom: the clause's second arm, restated as double entry on `iret_6_4__fstop`.

alloy.name: iret_6_4__v5_fault_then_false_rejects
alloy.note: THE CLAUSE'S ORDER, DRAWN: a faulting alpha test first in the source and a false one after it, both hoisted, reject in every order and record nothing. Under a short-circuit at the first filter that is not true this run is UNSAT, which `RunAlloy` fails.

alloy.name: rlow_5_5__v5_hoist_sound
alloy.note: HOISTING AND PROBING ARE SOUND for an artefact that does not lie: filters on decided conjuncts leave the decision of a positive and of a `no` pattern, and the record, unchanged. Admitting a nullable filter breaks it (TEETH). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: iret_6_4__admits
idris.note: A fact of the node's schema passing all its tests; the short-circuit is a Bool `&&`.

idris.name: iret_6_4__dispatch_assert
idris.note: ALPHA DISPATCH ON ASSERT: for each alpha node, in position order, evaluate the tests; on pass insert the fact and right-activate every chain. The clause's 'every alpha node registered for the schema': the schema check is the first test, so visiting every node is the same dispatch.

idris.name: Iret_6_4__dispatch_inv
idris.note: Midway through alpha dispatch: the memories of the alphas still to visit show the old working memory, the others the new; all distinct; every chain consistent with the memories as they stand.

idris.name: iret_19_1__insert_view
idris.note: INSERTING A FRESH FACT keeps the view: working memory stays distinct, and the dispatch runs from every alpha showing the old working memory to every alpha showing the new.

idris.name: iret_6_4__admits_some
idris.note: A dangling alpha reference admits nothing, so an admitting reference resolves.

idris.name: iret_6_4__dispatch_assert_hit
idris.note: ONE ALPHA VISITED ON ASSERT, admitting the fact, keeps the invariant: the fact enters that memory, which now shows the new working memory, and every chain is right-activated from it.

idris.name: iret_6_4__dispatch_assert_inv
idris.note: ALPHA DISPATCH ON ASSERT keeps the invariant over any distinct list of alphas to visit.

idris.name: iret_6_4__dispatch_assert_miss
idris.note: ONE ALPHA VISITED ON ASSERT, not admitting the fact, keeps the invariant: nothing changes, and that memory already shows the new working memory.

idris.name: iret_6_4__dispatch_finish
idris.note: After a dispatch every alpha memory shows the new working memory.

idris.name: iret_6_4__dispatch_assert_ordered
idris.note: ALPHA DISPATCH ON ASSERT keeps the order.

idris.name: iret_6_4__dispatch_assert_ordered_step
idris.note: One alpha visited on assert, admitting the fact, keeps every terminal in agenda order.

idris.name: iret_6_4__dispatch_inv_live
idris.note: Midway through a dispatch every alpha memory holds facts of the old or of the new working memory, so of any working memory containing both.

idris.name: iret_6_4__dispatch_assert_length
idris.note: The assert's dispatch keeps the number of chains.

idris.name: iret_6_4__admits_same
idris.note: Alphas of one shape admit the same facts.

idris.name: iret_6_4__dispatch_assert_shape
idris.note: ALPHA DISPATCH ON ASSERT keeps every shape: the alphas', and each chain's nodes and actions.

idris.name: iret_6_4__dispatch_assert_evolves
idris.note: The assert's dispatch creates only matches holding the fact.
